ranked_findings: 1. Five more hashes join MUM in the key-free class (a fixed pair collides for EVERY seed, eps = 1), all confirmed by independent re-implementations validated against the SMHasher3 verification values: CityHash-64 (0 bits, 8-byte pair; the seed enters only through a bijective final HashLen16, proved with an explicit inverse; 2^32/2^32 and 2^30/2^30), FarmHash-64 NA (0 bits, same structure; 8-byte pair 2^30/2^30, plus closed-form 32-byte multicollisions with no search), MuseAir v0.3 (1.09 bits at 17 B, 1.58 at 24 B; all four variants; passes SMHasher3 250/250), gxhash v3.5.0 (1.58 bits, 24-byte pair; Peters' open issue #83 reproduced), MurmurHash3 x64_128 (1.58 bits, 24-byte pair, EXHAUSTIVE over the entire 2^32 seed space; 128-bit output buys nothing). For CityHash/FarmHash/gxhash eps is exactly 0 or 1 for every pair, so the seed contributes nothing to collision resistance at any length.

2. komihash is not '>= 32': the 64-byte lane-tie pair collides for 91.06% of all seeds (verified 0.910597 +- 9e-6 at 2^30; claim 0.910588 at 2^32), bits = log2(8/0.9106) = 3.14. Mechanism (derived, and the 0.642 + 0.358 x 3/4 model matches to four digits): the 64-byte loop builds its eight lane states from the two secret words by XOR with PUBLIC IV constants, so setting words 1,5 = words 0,4 ^ (IV2, IV6) makes two lanes compute the same 128-bit product for every seed, and the loop's XOR collapse discards the low halves; flipping bit 0 of words 0 and 1 survives unless a carry changes the high half. Holds for every length 64..127 (identical trailing bytes), 0/2^20 at >= 128 B, nothing above ~2^-24 below 64 B (5333-cell scan). komihash passes SMHasher3 250/250 and the paper's own SeedDifferential test at 2^30 seeds.

3. The paper's SeedDifferential test detects only the multiply-fold class: every non-proven hash it passes at 2^30 seeds (komihash, t1ha2-64/128, FarmHash-64.NA, CityHash-64, a5hash, gxhash-64, rust-ahash, MurmurHash3-128 per tools/bench/results/MANIFEST.md) now has a verified pair between 2^-46.7 and 1. Passing it is necessary, not sufficient; only Polymur, ChainHash and the polynomial hashes in that list carry a bound.

4. t1ha2-64 scores 31.0, the wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3 tier: a 16-byte vs 11-byte pair (both L = 2) collides at 2^-30.0 (exact 2^-26-dense seed class x conditional 2^-4.000; direct 28/2^35 + 1/2^30 = 2^-30.19). New trail class: for 9..16-byte messages the first word meets only the PUBLIC length in its 128-bit multiply, so the seed enters through one product whose low word is XORed and high word added; a 64-step carry-pattern DP finds the cheapest add/xor pattern. A second pair (13 vs 16 B) verified at 2^-31.0 over 2^36 uniform seeds. Caveat: the 31.0 relies on unequal lengths; the best equal-length (16/16) pair known is 2^-44.85 (unverified) -> 45.9*. L = 1 is proved state-collision-free; L >= 3 and > 32 B null at 2^-26 per cell.

5. rust-ahash (AES path, aHash 0.8): 22.5 bits. A 56-byte pair collides at 2^-19.65 (pooled 2616/2^31; 64-byte variant 5011/2^32 = 2^-19.71) over the full 256-bit RandomState, via a 3-S-box inverse-AES differential whose additive shadow the shuffle constant routes back onto itself (predicted 2^-19.69). Three independent implementations agree. The fallback path (what a default x86-64 cargo build runs; passes SMHasher3 250/250) inherits the wyhash-type fold: (M,M) at 16 B gives 55/2^32 = 2^-26.2 -> 27.2 bits, claimant only, not re-measured.

6. SpookyHash2-64 and -128: 6.16 bits. A 286-byte pair collides on the full 768-bit state for exactly half of all seeds (2^30 seeds with h1 = h2 = seed and 2^28 independent 128-bit seeds; the predictor 'bit 63 of s11 before the rotl 46' matched 100% for both verifiers). Cause: V2's End adds the final block unmixed, so a +2^63 injected at Mix step 11 leaves only s10 ^ 2^63 and s11 +- 2^45, both cancelled by End words 10 and 11. The 128-bit native seed does not help; 1/2 is the ceiling for single-step injections (the injected word is always rotated once).

7. a5hash v5.21: 48.3 bits (an upper bound on the score). The seed expansion is one 64x64 multiply of two constants carrying the odd and even seed bits, so low-word values with 156800 preimages exist (exact 2-adic enumeration over all 2^64 seeds, every seed re-hashed by two agents), and a dead first block (word 0 == s1_0) frees word 1: 23-byte pair at exactly 2^-46.74 = 2^17 x ideal; 8-byte pair at 2^-51.17 (7291 seeds, both messages hash to 0). Passes SMHasher3 250/250. a5hash-128 is worse than its 64-bit sibling: Seed3..Seed8 are PUBLIC, so key-free full-128-bit pairs exist from 25 bytes (2^22/2^22, claimant only).

8. Published breaks were reproduced, not merely cited: Peters 2023 (CityHash64 strings 10/10 -> 0x539 on v1.0.3; FarmHash64 strings 10/10 -> 1337 on the SMHasher3 code; MurmurHash3_x86_32 pair 2^20/2^20; gxhash issue #83 pair 2^30/2^30) and Aumasson-Bernstein-Bosslet 29C3 2012 (CityHash v1.0.3 PoC rebuilt from the web archive, 8/8; the MurmurHash top-bit mechanism carried to x64_128, exhaustive over 2^32 seeds). The 2012/2023 CityHash strings do NOT collide under the SMHasher3 v1.1.1 code (HashLen0to16/17to32 were rewritten); the structural property persists and new v1.1.1 pairs were constructed.

9. Larger secrets do not rescue any of them where they exist: CityHash64WithSeeds (2^28 and 2^30 random 128-bit pairs), FarmHash Hash64WithSeeds (2^24), SpookyHash's 128-bit seed (2^28, still 1/2), rust-ahash's full 256-bit RandomState (the model measured), gxhash's HashMap RandomState (by reading hasher.rs, not executed), komihash under a uniform 128-bit preseed 0.875 (claimant only). MurmurHash3 (32-bit seed), MuseAir, a5hash and t1ha2_atonce offer none.

10. Failure taxonomy across the ten (useful as the paper's framing): (i) seed-last designs (CityHash, FarmHash, gxhash) -> eps in {0,1}, a public-function collision problem; (ii) some words injected through a public function only (MuseAir tail, a5hash-128 Seed3..8, MUM) -> key-free; (iii) seed as IV with XOR injection through public bijections (MurmurHash3) -> deterministic top-bit trails; (iv) lane states = secret ^ public constant (komihash) -> lane ties; (v) unmixed final additions (SpookyHash V2) -> late-injection cancellation at 1/2; (vi) hi^lo folds (wyhash, XXH3, ahash fallback) -> 2^-27; (vii) add/xor carry patterns on a single seed product (t1ha2) -> 2^-30; (viii) weak seed expansion + dead multiply (a5hash) -> 2^-47.

11. The 'SMHasher3-strong' premise holds strictly (250/250 upstream) only for komihash (3.1), a5hash (48.3), MuseAir (1.1) and the ahash fallback (27.2*); upstream SMHasher3 already fails CityHash-64 and FarmHash-64.NA (205/250), MurmurHash3-128 (163/250), gxhash-64 (226/250), rust-ahash AES (242/250), SpookyHash2-64 (244/250) and t1ha2-64 (247/250), all on seed tests. Even so, the bits scores of the four clean passers span 1.1 to 48.3 against the 64 their width suggests.

res.structure_notes: t1ha2_atonce: a = seed, b = len. len <= 32: up to four mixup64(&X,&Y,w,prime): (l,h) = 128-bit (Y+w)*prime, X ^= l, Y += h; then final64(a,b) = mux64(((a+ROTR(b,41))*P0) ^ ((ROTR(a,23)+b)*P6), P5) with mux64 = lo^hi of a 128-bit product by a public prime. len > 32: 4-word state (c,d derived from seed,len), 32-byte UPDATE with 64-bit bijective multiplies by public primes XORed into state, squash, then the same tail. Key fact: for len 9..16 (L = 2 words) word 0 enters as (len + w0)*P2 with b = len PUBLIC, so a = seed ^ l(w0), B = len + h(w0) with l,h attacker-known (128-bit product is injective in w0, so no key-free pair); the tail t enters as u = a + t, (L,H) = u*P1, final state (a + H, B ^ L). A fixed pair collides on the state iff (i) Da + (H* - H) = 0 (hi-word of du*P1 plus a carry plus a wrap event on u + du) and (ii) (L + D) ^ L = B ^ B* with D = du*P1 mod 2^64: ONE seed-dependent add/xor carry pattern (L uniform) whose minimum weight, jointly consistent with the public carry pattern of B + K (K = B* - B), is found by a 64-step DP. The attacker tunes Da (signed-digit differences of l, each non-top digit costs 1/2 for the sign of the additive a-difference; the top bit 2^63 is free), du, the x-wrap variant and the length offset len* - len in [-7,7] (cross-length pairs, free extra K choices), then realises w0 via preimages of hi(x*P2). The seed-independent parts are exact; the cost is 2^-(wt(E) + #digits + wrap). Best realisable trail: dp 26 + 4 digits + ~0 wrap = 2^-30.0. Why L = 2 is the sweet spot: len <= 8 (L = 1): b_final = len ^ lo((seed+v)*P1) is a bijection of v, so two distinct messages NEVER collide on the state, only in final64 (generic ~2^-64) — proved. L >= 3: the first word enters as seed + w0 (not public), so a trail needs two independent random carry patterns (cost ~doubles; ~2^-60+). len > 32: any single-block state collision is impossible (w0/w1 uniquely feed c_new/d_new; the (w2,w3) <-> (c13,d02) cancellation loop shifts bit positions by -11 mod 64 and never closes), and two-block trails pay >= 2 bits per bit position in that loop; top-bit differences in the block words leave non-top additive differences in c/d that squash scrambles. No dead-operand weak-seed class helps (the dead operand is state+word, distinct messages cannot both be dead). Attacks needing only public constants: none found (every message word meets the seed through an injective 128-bit product or the seed itself). No larger-secret interface exists for t1ha2_atonce (the 128-bit-seed t1ha2 streaming/2x64 variants were not analysed; the trail uses only the len<=16 path, which in t1ha2_atonce128 is the same first mixup but a different tail, so it does not transfer as is).

res.bottle_vs_reality: The bottle: t1ha2 is a 64-bit hash with a 64-bit seed that passes SMHasher/SMHasher3, which implicitly suggests a fixed message pair should collide with probability about 2^-64 over a random seed. Reality: because the first word of a 9..16-byte message meets only the public length (b = len) in its 128-bit multiply, the seed enters the final state through a single 128-bit product whose low word is XORed and high word added, and a fixed pair of messages (16 bytes vs 11 bytes) collides for a 2^-30.0 fraction of all 64-bit seeds (measured: 1.05M collisions on the 2^-26 seed class at 2^24 conditional samples; 12 collisions in 2^34 uniform seeds). That is bits = 31.0 by the paper's metric (L = 2 words), in the same tier as wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3 (~27-29) and 33 bits below the width. Unlike MUM there is no key-free pair (every word meets the seed through an injective product), so t1ha2 is not 0 bits, and 1..8-byte messages are provably state-collision-free.
res.caveats: (1) All eps values are measured lower bounds for the specific pair via exact conditional sampling on the seed class (class density is exact since L is a bijective image of the seed) plus a direct uniform run; other collision events for the same pair add at most a negligible amount. (2) The direct 2^34 run gave 12 collisions (2^-30.42) vs 16 expected at 2^-30.00; the conditional estimate (2^-30.00 +- 0.01) is the precise one. (3) The trail-search coverage is stated exactly: all 1-, 2-, 3-digit signed-digit word-0 differences with all du/wrap/length-offset variants (159M DP runs) and a random sample of 40M 4-digit routes (10 x 4M, seeds 1..10); DP estimates 29.01 existed but were infeasible (the fixed bits of B forced the x + d0 wrap the DP assumed away); 5+ digit routes were not explored, so a slightly better pair (perhaps 1-2 bits) may exist — bits = 31.0 is 'best found', not a proof of optimality. (4) The L=1 statement (no state collision) is proved; the L>=3 and >32-byte-path statements (two independent carry patterns; non-closing rotation loop) are analytic arguments backed only by the 2^-26-resolution generic scan, not exhaustive. (5) Cross-length pair: m is 16 bytes and m2 is 11 bytes; both are 2 words, and the same family gives an equal-length 16/16 pair at 2^-44.85 and a 16/13 pair at 2^-31.0. (6) Only t1ha2_atonce (64-bit) was analysed, not t1ha2_atonce128, the streaming variant, t1ha0/t1ha1. (7) No timing claims.

res.structure_notes: Seed interface is uint32_t (h1 = h2 = (uint32_t)seed; SMHasher3's 64-bit seed_t is truncated, FLAG_HASH_SMALL_SEED), so the secret is 32 bits and every pair below was checked over ALL 2^32 seeds. Per 16-byte block: h1 ^= g1(k1); h1 = rotl(h1,27); h1 += h2; h1 = 5*h1+c; h2 ^= g2(k2); h2 = rotl(h2,31); h2 += h1; h2 = 5*h2+c, with g1(k) = rotl(k*c1,31)*c2 and g2(k) = rotl(k*c2,33)*c1 public bijections. Tail: h2 ^= g2(k2_tail) (bytes 8..14, at most 7 bytes), h1 ^= g1(k1_tail). Finalization: h1 ^= len; h2 ^= len; then a bijection of the 128-bit state. Message words meet the secret only through XOR of a public bijection into the state, so the 2012 MurmurHash2 top-bit argument applies: x ^ 2^63 == x + 2^63, hence a state difference of 2^63 is preserved by += h, by *5+c (5*2^63 = 2^63 mod 2^64) and cancelled by XOR; a g1 difference of 2^36 becomes 2^63 after rotl 27, a g2 difference of 2^32 becomes 2^63 after rotl 31. One block maps the state difference (d1,d2) in {0,2^63}^2 to (r1^d2, r2^r1^d2) with r1, r2 freely chosen through the message differences. Two blocks reach (0,0) (32-byte pair); one block reaches (2^63, 0), which a full 8-byte k1 tail cancels with g1 difference 2^63 (24-byte pair). Nothing shorter is deterministic: for <=15-byte messages the state is (seed ^ g1(k1) ^ len, seed ^ g2(k2) ^ len), so a collision is seed-independent and needs g2(k2)^g2(k2') = len^len' with both k2 words <= 7 bytes; exactly, g2inv(g2(k)^delta) = k + D with D = (rotr(eps*c1^-1,33) + c - o*2^31)*c2^-1 (eps = (y^delta)-y, c,o carry flags; identity verified on 2^24 random inputs, 0 mismatches), and min |D| over the feasible deltas is 2^56.6 > 2^56, so no such pair exists; one length <= 8 needs g2inv(delta) < 2^56 but all are >= 2^60. Same lengths are injective. 16 bytes vs shorter: the h1 lane needs (5*(rotl(s^A,27)+s)+C) ^ s = const over seeds s, and flipping bit 0 of s changes the inner sum by +-2^27+-1, never mapping to a +-1 change, so at most half the seeds can satisfy it (eps <= 1/2, bits >= 2). L = 1: h2 = seed ^ len, so different lengths never collide and equal lengths are injective (eps = 0). Block + <8-byte tail cannot cancel 2^63 (g1 constant 2^61); block + 9..15-byte tails with different lengths need g2 constants for 2^63^(len^len'), which only fit for len^len' in {2,6,14}, giving 25..31-byte pairs (L = 4), no better than 32 bytes. No fold sites, no weak-seed classes needed: every result is key-free.

The 32-bit variant scores 0 (8-byte universal pair, Peters' published pair reproduced) and x86_128 scores 2 (32-byte universal pair). No larger secret interface exists to escape to, no public constants beyond c1, c2 are needed, and the attack costs four multiplications.

res.structure_notes: Secret: Seed1 = IV1 ^ (seed & 0x5555..), Seed5 = IV5 ^ (seed & 0xAAAA..) (32 seed bits each), then one HASHROUND (128-bit multiply, S5 += hi, S1 = lo ^ S5). Every message word is XORed into one operand of a 64x64->128 multiply whose other operand is secret; no word passes through a public-only function (no MUM-style rho pair). Short paths (<64 bytes) chain (S1,S5) through full 128-bit products (S1 = lo ^ (S5+hi), S5 += hi), so a state collision needs both lo and hi equal and the hi^lo-type 2^-27 fold differential does not apply; the only sub-generic structure there is the dead multiply (r2h = S5 ^ tail = 0 or r1h = S1 ^ word0 = 0), a weak-seed class of density ~2^-64 per fixed pair. The 64-byte loop (len >= 64) is the weak spot: it derives eight lane states from the two secrets by XOR with PUBLIC constants (S2 = IV2^S1, S3 = IV3^S1, S4 = IV4^S1, S6 = IV6^S5, S7 = IV7^S5, S8 = IV8^S5), computes per lane P_i = (S_i ^ m_{i-1}) * (S_{i+4} ^ m_{i+3}) with S_i = lo_i, S_{i+4} += hi_i, XORs lanes crosswise, and when the loop exits (len < 128) collapses the state to S5f = XOR_i (c_i + hi_i) (c_1 = S5, c_2 = S5^IV6, c_3 = S5^IV7, c_4 = S5^IV8) and S1f = (lo_1^lo_2^lo_3^lo_4) ^ S5f. Setting m1 = m0 ^ IV2 and m5 = m4 ^ IV6 makes P_1 = P_2 for EVERY seed, so lo_1 ^ lo_2 = 0 cancels the 64 bits of lo information; a pair differing only in lanes 1,2 collides iff (S5+h) ^ (S5^IV6+h) is unchanged, h = hi((S1^m0)(S5^m4)). Flipping bit 0 of m0 (and of m1 to keep the tie) changes the product by +-b (b = S5^m4), so h is unchanged iff no carry: Pr = 1 - E[b]/2^64; S5 after the init round has skewed top bits (P[bit63]=0.28, P[bit62]=0.57), so m4 = bitwise majority of S5 (0x5ea1c0c1a4ddf9f0) gives Pr = 0.642. Otherwise h' = h+-1, and because IV6 = ..0C6C has two trailing zero bits the two sums agree in bits 0-1 and differ in bit 2, so the increment flips identical patterns iff the low two bits of the smaller sum are not 11: Pr = 3/4. Predicted eps = 0.642 + 0.358*0.75 = 0.9106; measured 0.910588 at 2^32. The attack is independent of (S1,S5) (0.875 with a uniform 128-bit preseed state) and fails for >= 128 bytes because a second iteration needs the full 512-bit lane state, not only its XOR collapse (0/2^20 at 128, 192, 256, 1000 bytes).

res.structure_notes: Seed expansion: s1_0||s2_0 = umul128((C2^len)^(seed&0xAAAA..), (C1^len)^(seed&0x5555..)) Tail 1..16 bytes: s1^=A, s2^=B with A=u32(0)<<32|u32(len-4), B=u32(mo*4)<<32|u32(len-4-mo*4), mo=len>>3 (len 4..7 have A==B, len 8 has B=swap32(A)). Final: (l,h)=umul128(s1,s2); (l2,h2)=umul128(l^0x5555..,h); return l2^h2. Every message word is XORed with secret state before any multiply, so the 64-bit variant has no public-function (rho) path and the 2012 universal multicollisions do not apply. The exploitable structure is the DEAD MULTIPLY: W0^s1==0 in a block zeroes the product and makes the state (v1,v2) independent of W1; s1^A==0 in the tail makes the hash 0 independent of B. A fixed pair (A,B)/(A,B') thus collides for every seed with s1_0==A. The seed expansion is far from uniform: s1_0 = p*q mod 2^64 with p=(C2^len)^oddbits(seed), q=(C1^len)^evenbits(seed); bit j of p*q depends only on bits<=j and at each j exactly one of p_j,q_j is a free seed bit, so ALL seeds with s1_0==T are enumerated exactly by 2-adic lifting (lift.c); for even T the population branches (critical branching process) and T can be CHOSEN by a beam search over its bits to have 10^3..10^5+ preimages instead of ~1. Odd lengths (p even; C2^23 has 5 trailing zeros) are best. Secondary, measured but not needed: the tail hyperbola class (s1^A)(s2^B)<2^64 => h=0 => hash 0 (mass ~45*2^-64 for uniform state); s2_0=hi(pq) is lumpy (densest top-k-bit cell has 2^k*Pr = 2^2.1, 2^3.0, 2^4.2, 2^5.1, 2^5.5 at k=4,12,20,32,36; hisearch), so the s2_0==B dead class is only ~2^8-2^10 seeds.

res.structure_notes: PROVED (from the source): gxhash(m, seed) = F_seed(C(m)) where C = compress_all(m) contains NO seed, and F_seed(x) = finalize(aesenc(x, seed||seed)) is three public-key AES rounds after the seed XOR, i.e. a bijection of 128-bit blocks for every seed. Hence for every fixed pair eps(m,m') = 1 if C(m) = C(m') and, for the 128-bit output, exactly 0 otherwise: the seed has no influence on WHICH pairs collide, and no seed size (the HashMap path uses a 128-bit RandomState) changes that. C is trivially collidable in constant time because every branch ends in an XOR of independently processed message parts: len<=16: C = zeropad(m)+len bytewise (injective at fixed len, but a k<16-byte message m collides with the 16-byte message m16[i] = (i<k ? m[i] : 0) + k - 16); 17..32 bytes: C = SR(SB(hv)) XOR P2(v0) with hv = get_partial(m[0:len-16]), v0 = m[len-16:len], P2 = two public rounds (K0,K1): pick hv != hv', set v0' = P2^{-1}(P2(v0) ^ SR(SB(hv)) ^ SR(SB(hv'))); 33..64 bytes: v0 <- aesenc(v0, v1) [<- aesenc(., v2)], so a change of v0 is cancelled by v1' = v1 ^ MC(SR(SB(v0))) ^ MC(SR(SB(v0'))); >64 bytes: leading blocks hv <- aesenc(hv, block) (same cancellation) and 8-block groups tmp1 = aesenc(aesenc(aesenc(g0,g2),g4),g6), tmp2 likewise on odd blocks (change g0, fix g2 or g6). Multicollisions of any size K: B_i = P2^{-1}(T ^ SR(SB(A_i))) at 32 bytes (4096-way demonstrated, all members equal for every seed). Injection points where a message word meets the secret: none; the only secret-dependent operation is the single XOR of seed||seed after compression (64 bits of entropy duplicated into both halves), followed by public rounds. For the 64-bit truncation and pairs with C(m) != C(m') (only possible at same length <= 16 bytes): argued (not proved) eps <~ 2^-64: a single-active-byte difference is provably a non-collision (fully active after two rounds), and a truncated collision needs 8 specific bytes of the round-2 difference to vanish (~2^-16 per active MixColumns column); measured 0 in 98 cells x 2^26 seeds.

res.bottle_vs_reality: The README (v3.5.0, section Security) says 'GxHash is seeded (with seed randomization) to improve DOS resistance and uses a wide (128-bit) internal state to improve multicollision resistance. Yet, such resistances are just basic safeguards', exports a 'DOS-resistant' gxhash::HashMap, and passes all SMHasher3 tests (SMHasher3 results table: gxhash-64 and gxhash both pass). In reality the seed is XORed in once AFTER the entire message has been compressed by a public, seed-free function C, and is followed only by a public bijection, so collisions are a property of C alone: eps is exactly 1 or (for 128 bits) exactly 0 for every pair, whatever the seed, and C collides in constant time at every length >= 17 bytes, across lengths (any k<16-byte message has a 16-byte twin), and with arbitrary-size multicollisions. The seed randomization therefore provides no DoS resistance at all: bits = log2(3) = 1.58 for the 24-byte pair (2.0 for the 32-byte pair under the multiple-of-16 convention, 1.0 for the cross-length 15-vs-16 byte pair), i.e. in the MUM class, versus the 64 the seed width and the 'DOS-resistant' label suggest. The weakness was reported upstream by Orson Peters in June 2024 (issue #83) and remains open.

res.structure_notes: AES path: enc=(k0,k1), sum=(k2,k3), key=enc^sum. hash_in(v): enc <- aesdec(enc)^v [InvShiftRows,InvSubBytes,InvMixColumns then XOR v]; sum <- shuffle(sum)+v [fixed 16-byte permutation MASK, then two 64-bit lane additions]. First hash_in is on (len,0), then enc[0]+=len. Lengths 1-16: one data block (no cancellation possible); 17-32: blocks [0,16),[len-16,len); 33-64: [0,16),[16,32),[len-32,len-16),[len-16,len); >64: four AES lanes current[i] (key, one aesenc/aesdec of the last 64 bytes, then aesdec per 16-byte block) plus two additive lanes sum[0]=key, sum[1]=~key, all six then hash_in'ed. finish: c=aesenc(sum)^enc; c=aesdec(c)^key; c=aesdec(c)^c_prev; output = low 64 bits. Every message word meets key-derived state before any nonlinearity, so there is no public-only function of the message (no key-free/rho pair as for MUM). Differences: a block XOR-difference d enters enc as XOR and sum as an additive lane difference; a single active byte costs one inverse-S-box transition (<=4/256) and InvMixColumns spreads it to a full column; the shuffle constant sends every byte b OUTSIDE the InvShiftRows column of b, maps no column to a column and no three bytes of any column into one column, so (support_search.py, exhaustive at the byte-support level) NO 2-block byte-local trail exists for any 1-4 active bytes, and no 3-block trail with 1+1 S-boxes. The cheapest trails have 3 S-boxes: two 3-block trails (eps1={0,10},eps2={2} and eps1={8,15},eps2={10}) and one 4-block trail (eps1={6},eps2={14},eps3={7}; value level best 2^-21.0). Fallback path: buffer=k1, pad=k0, extra_keys=(k2,k3); per 16-byte block combined=fold(w0^k2, w1^k3) with fold = lo64^hi64 of the 128-bit product, buffer=rotl((buffer+pad)^combined,23); 9-16-byte messages are one such block, so the pair collides exactly when the fold does (the same XOR multiply-fold as wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3); <=8-byte messages give only 32-bit operand control (u32 at 0, u32 at len-4). Dead-operand weak keys (w0^k2=0) have density 2^-64 only.

res.structure_notes: Two paths. SHORT (< 192 bytes): state (a,b,c,d) = (seed, seed, K, K) with K = 0xdeadbeefdeadbeef; per 32-byte block c += w0; d += w1; ShortMix(a,b,c,d); a += w2; b += w3; a 16..31-byte remainder does c += w0; d += w1; ShortMix; the last 0..15 bytes are packed into c and d together with d += len<<56 (remainder 0: c += K; d += K); ShortEnd (11 add-rotate-xor steps); output a. Every message word meets the seed inside ShortMix (12 steps, each rotate/add/xor over 4 words) or ShortEnd; the attacker adds an arbitrary 256-bit vector to the full state between consecutive ShortMix calls (w2,w3 of block i and w0,w1 of block i+1), so a seed-independent pair needs a deterministic additive differential through one whole ShortMix (or a ShortEnd differential to h0). Measured: for all 9082 low-weight additive input diffs (every single bit, every same-word bit pair, every cross-word pair containing a top bit) the most frequent additive output difference of ShortMix already falls below 2^-11 by step 5 of 12; the same diffs into ShortEnd give 0 h0-collisions at 2^14 samples each. The first ShortMix sees (seed, seed, known, known) but that only makes step 1 deterministic. LONG (>= 192 bytes): 12-word state h0=h3=h6=h9=seed1, h1=h4=h7=h10=seed2, h2=h5=h8=h11=K; Mix step i: s_i += w_i; s_{i+2} ^= s_{i+10}; s_{i+11} ^= s_i; s_i = rotl(s_i, r_i); s_{i+11} += s_{i+1}; then V2's End does h_i += data_i on the zero-padded final block (buf[95] = remainder) followed by 3 EndPartial rounds. The message word of step 11 is the last thing that touches the state before End's plain additions: w11 += 2^63 gives s10 += 2^63 exactly (XOR of a top-bit difference) and s11 += +-2^45 (the rotl by 46 of a top-bit difference; sign = bit 63 of s11 before the rotate). Both residues are cancelled by End word 10 (+2^63) and End word 11 (-2^45, bytes 88..94 of the End block are message bytes, so the remainder must be >= 94): the entire 768-bit state collides with probability exactly Pr[that bit = 0] = 1/2 over the seed, for both the 64-bit and the 128-bit output and for both seed models. No injection can do better than 1/2 in this style: every s_i is rotated inside its own step and the rotation of a nonzero additive difference of a uniformly random word is never deterministic. Injecting earlier (block 1 step 11) leaves a sparse 'wave' that crosses a block at roughly 1 condition per step (~13 bits) and never dies, so 286 bytes at 1/2 is the best of the family. SpookyHash V1's End runs a Mix over the final block instead of adding it, which is exactly what this trail needs to be absent (analysis only, not measured).

res.bottle_vs_reality: SpookyHash V2 passes SMHasher3 and advertises a 128-bit state, 64/128-bit outputs, a 128-bit seed and a designer's note that 'every input bit causes at least 128 bits of entropy before 96 other bytes are combined'; a random-seed collision probability of 2^-64 (64-bit output) would be the implied precision, and the 64-bit seed model would put it at bits ~ 64 + log2 L. Reality: because V2 replaced the final Mix of the last block by twelve plain additions (h_i += data_i), the last Mix step's word is the only thing standing between the attacker and an additive cancellation, and that step is a single top-bit XOR plus one rotate. A fixed 286-byte pair (block-2 word 11 += 2^63, End word 10 += 2^63, End word 11 -= 2^45) collides on the full 768-bit state, hence on both the 64- and 128-bit outputs, for exactly half of all seeds (2^30 seeds: 536868916 collisions; 2^28 independent 128-bit seeds: same rate). bits = log2(35.75 / 2^-1) = 6.16, i.e. the hash offers about 6 bits of precision in the paper's metric against 57-64 for the proven hashes and ~27-29 for wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3; only MUM (0 bits) is worse. The larger 128-bit native seed does not help (the trail is seed-independent), and there is no public-constant-only attack beyond this (none is needed). The short path (< 192 bytes) showed nothing at the resolutions run (2^-26 per generic cell, 2^-14 per ShortEnd diff, ShortMix determinism gone by step 5), so the weakness is specifically the V2 finalisation of long messages.

Null scans: clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o scan scan.cpp && ./scan 26 16 "8,16,24,32,40,48,56,64,12,15,20,31,47,63" (run on hardware.normalcomputing.net, 16 threads; experiment/spookyhash2-64/scan26.log, copied to scan26_server.log); clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -include array -o diffsearch diffsearch.cpp && ./diffsearch 0 2048 (ShortMix) && ./diffsearch 1 16384 (ShortEnd).
res.caveats: (1) The 1/2 ceiling is proved only for single-step injections cancelled by End; multi-word injections within the last Mix were analysed by hand (they add rotate conditions, so cost >= 1 bit each) but not searched exhaustively. (2) Short path (< 192 bytes): null at the stated resolutions only (generic cells 2^26 seeds; ShortEnd diffs 2^14 samples; ShortMix determinism scan N=2048 per step); no automated signed-difference trail search was run, so a ShortMix/ShortEnd trail of probability between 2^-64 and ~2^-27 is not excluded; the score is unaffected because bits is a min over L and the long-path pair already gives 6.16. (3) The cross-block 'wave' cost (~13 bits per Mix block) is a hand estimate, not measured. (4) SpookyHash V1 (End = Mix of the last block) is stated not to admit this trail by structure; not measured. (5) Length in words is 35.75 (286 bytes); reported as 36. (6) The same pair breaks SpookyHash2_128 (full state collision) with the same 2^-1 rate; SpookyHash2_32 likewise. (7) No timing claims; the server was used only for the 2^26 site scan.

pair.example_seed: 0x0000000000000004 (h1 = h2 = 4; both messages hash to 0xe3f63e3f415763ac, and the full 128-bit outputs agree)
pair.notes: 286 bytes = 35.75 words (2 Mix blocks + 94-byte End block); M2 = M with byte 191 ^= 0x80 (block-2 word 11 += 2^63), byte 279 ^= 0x80 (End word 10 += 2^63), byte 285 bit 5 cleared (End word 11 -= 2^45). Collides iff bit 63 of s11 before the step-11 rotate is 0: rate 2^-1.0000 at 2^30 seeds with h1=h2=seed, and 2^-1.0000 at 2^28 independent 128-bit seeds (longpair.cpp mode 1). Every collision is a full 768-bit state collision, so it collides the 128-bit output too. Seed-independent in the sense that the trail holds for any seed distribution; each fixed pair covers exactly the seeds with one sign, so 1/2 is the ceiling for a single pair (proved for single-step injections: the injected word is always rotated within its step). Shortest possible length for the trail: the -2^45 cancellation needs End bytes up to 93, i.e. remainder 94, length 192+94.
pair.conditional_on: none (unconditional over the seed; the 1/2 is Pr[bit 63 of the pre-rotate s11 = 0])

All measured numbers agree with the claim (rate 2^-1, count 536868916 vs my 536880211 at 2^30, within statistical error).
